note:
Field Delimiter adds a 'Field Delimiter' textfield to a field formatter on MULTI-VALUE fields (via hook_field_formatter_third_party_settings_form). No configure route (configure=null), no permissions, no Drush, no plugins. Its only persistent state is a third-party setting field_delimiter.delimiter stored on a formatter component in an entity_view_display config entity: core.entity_view_display... -> content..third_party_settings.field_delimiter.delimiter (schema field.formatter.third_party.field_delimiter). hook_preprocess_field appends the XSS-filtered delimiter (allowing only br/hr/span/img/wbr) as a #suffix on each item except the last, when 2+ items. Medium cases read back which field has a delimiter and its value; hard cases set a text delimiter (' / ') and an HTML delimiter ('
') on a namespaced multi-value field, verified against the live entity_view_display.

evals.prompt: I enabled field_delimiter but see no settings page. How do I actually put a comma between the values of a multi-value field on a Drupal 11 site, and where is that choice stored?
evals.expected_output: There is no configure route. On the entity's Manage display, open the multi-value field's formatter cog and fill in the 'Field Delimiter' textfield, Update, Save. It is stored as a third-party setting on that field's formatter component: core.entity_view_display.<entity>.<bundle>.<view_mode> -> content.<field>.third_party_settings.field_delimiter.delimiter.

evals.prompt: On which fields does the field_delimiter 'Field Delimiter' setting appear? Does it work on a single-value field?
evals.expected_output: The setting only appears for multi-value fields (fields whose storage isMultiple(), i.e. cardinality > 1 or unlimited). It has no effect on a single-value field, and hook_preprocess_field also bails when there are fewer than 2 items.

evals.prompt: How does field_delimiter actually insert the delimiter between rendered field values, and what HTML is allowed in the delimiter?
evals.expected_output: hook_preprocess_field() sets $item['content']['#suffix'] to the delimiter on every rendered item except the last (when there are 2+ items). The delimiter is passed through Xss::filter allowing only the tags br, hr, span, img, wbr.

evals.prompt: On this site, the Article content type has a multi-value field whose default-view-mode formatter uses field_delimiter to separate values. Inspect the live view display and tell me the exact delimiter string configured.
evals.expected_output: The delimiter is ' ~fd~ ' (with surrounding spaces), stored at core.entity_view_display.node.article.default -> content.field_fdlm_tags.third_party_settings.field_delimiter.delimiter.

evals.prompt: The Article content type on this site has a multi-value field configured with a field_delimiter delimiter on its default view-mode formatter. Inspect the live view-display configuration and give the machine name of that field.
evals.expected_output: The field is field_fdlm_tags: in core.entity_view_display.node.article.default its formatter component has third_party_settings.field_delimiter.delimiter set.

evals.prompt: On this site the Article content type has a multi-value field field_fdlm_task shown with the 'string' formatter in the default view mode. Using field_delimiter, configure that formatter so the field's values are separated by ' / ' (space slash space). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_view_display.node.article.default the field_fdlm_task component carries third_party_settings.field_delimiter.delimiter = ' / '. Set it on the view display component and save, or type it in the formatter's Field Delimiter box on Manage display.

evals.prompt:
The Article content type on this site has a multi-value field field_fdlm_list using the 'string' formatter in the default view mode. Using field_delimiter, make each value render on its own line by setting the delimiter to a literal
tag. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output:
In core.entity_view_display.node.article.default the field_fdlm_list component carries third_party_settings.field_delimiter.delimiter = '
' (br is one of the allowed tags, so it renders each value on a new line).
